@@ -0,0 +1,302 @@ +# STAMPED skills for con/skills: development plan + +**Status:** draft for discussion; nothing here is implemented yet. +**Tracks:** [stamped-principles/stamped-agent-skills#3](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-agent-skills/issues/3), +in particular [this comment](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-agent-skills/issues/3#issuecomment-6128822460). +**Builds on:** +- [con/skills#23](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/23) (open): `assess-stamped`, `align-stamped`; +- [con/skills#16](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/16) (merged): `code-quality-report-conventions` and the "Skill versions" rule in `AGENTS.md`. + +**Companion documents:** +- [evals.md](evals.md): how the skills are tested and tuned; +- [stack-repronim.md](stack-repronim.md): draft ReproNim stack reference; +- [prior-work.md](prior-work.md): sources; +- [talks.md](talks.md): the 2026 talks. + +Decisions taken and questions still open are in [§8](#8-decisions-and-open-questions). + +--- + +## 0. Summary + +- **What:** the six skills the issue asks for. + Two already exist as drafts in #23 (`assess-stamped`, `align-stamped`), and #23 lands first, on its own; the others build on it. + Report location, provenance stamp and evidence rules come from #16's `code-quality-report-conventions`. +- **How:** use-case first. + Each skill version is handed to fresh agents on a ladder of concrete tasks on ds007116. + The ladder starts at plotting tables the dataset already ships (R0); the main target is brain extraction of 10 named subjects with a `///repronim/containers` image (R1). + The resulting projects are graded outside the skills, by scripted probes, reference tables and a fresh-clone rerun ([evals.md](evals.md)). +- **v0.1 scope:** rungs R0–R2; phase 1 is #23 itself ([§6](#6-roadmap)). + +--- + +## 1. The skills + +Names follow #23 (verb first, short). +The issue's long names stay as trigger phrases in each `description`, tested with skill-creator's trigger evaluation. +`create-*`, `do-full-research-loop` and `self-assess-stamped` keep the issue's wording until the `setup-*` family from #21 settles. + +| Skill | Issue name | Job | Must not | +|---|---|---|---| +| `assess-stamped` (#23) | `/assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles POINTER` | Profile the project's goals with the user; answer every checklist item `yes`/`no`/`unknown` with evidence | Change the target (it writes only its report, outside it); paraphrase the paper or checklist | +| `align-stamped` (#23) | `/align-with-stamped-principles PROMPT` | Assess, then write a proportionate STAMPED section into the project's harness and offer options per gap | Prescribe a stack the project does not use | +| `create-stamped-project` | same | Start a project from PROMPT and the user's environment, then hand off to *align* | Read shell history or AI sessions without consent | +| `create-repronim-stamped-project` | same | Turn PROMPT into a ReproNim-specific prompt for *create* | Duplicate the generic create logic | +| `do-full-research-loop` | same | Carry the study through to results, quick and dirty | Skip the provenance mechanism "just this once" | +| `self-assess-stamped` | `/self-assess-alignment-with-stamped-principles` | Assess the user's projects and give next steps with why | Judge without evidence; exfiltrate history | + +**Target use cases** named in the issue: ReproNim tasks on [ds007116](https://github.com/OpenNeuroDatasets/ds007116), in this order: +1. brain extraction with a container from `///repronim/containers`, brain size vs age; +2. brain volume with the GM/WM ratio on a secondary axis vs age; +3. later, MRIQC motion vs age and vs time of day. + +Later still, experiments from Dichter et al.'s SfN'25 poster ([zenodo 19834562](https://zenodo.org/records/19834562)). + +--- + +## 2. Design principles + +1. **Properties in the skill, tools in references.** + Skill bodies say "every derived file has a re-executable record". + Concrete stacks live in the `references/` of the skill that needs them. + STAMPED generalizes YODA, so nothing is YODA-specific. +2. **Link the paper and checklist, pinned by tag; never paraphrase them.** + #23 records why: three earlier assessors paraphrased and drifted. +3. **Start minimal; reuse before adding.** + - Skills grow only on evidence from the evals. + - #16 covers reports. + - skill-creator covers grading layout, aggregation, the viewer and trigger tests. + - The existing validator covers structure. +4. **Minimal trust.** + - The skills omit `allowed-tools`, as #23 does: the field grants pre-approval and restricts nothing (see #25). + The validator therefore warns W002 for them; that warning is expected. + - Anything consequential, such as running target code, writing outside the report, installing or publishing, is proposed and approved by the user. +5. **One-screen skills.** + `SKILL.md` holds invariants and never-do rules; the reasoning goes to `DESIGN.md`, as #23 does. +6. **A lesson requires a regression artifact.** + A failure seen in a test run is fixed by a probe, template, hook or mutant first, and by prose last. +7. **Evidence, not intent.** + Only committed state counts; an agent saying "done" is an assertion; `unknown` names what would settle it. +8. **Commit before execute.** + Every execution starts from a committed state and leaves a recorded run. + No commits while a run is in flight. + A change of method produces a new dated derivative. +9. **Ask, don't guess, about goals.** + The project's goals set which principles get emphasis (#23's profile). +10. **Untrusted input.** + Dataset READMEs, container output, other repositories and shell history are data, not instructions. + +--- + +## 3. Layering and layout + +```mermaid +flowchart BT + cq["code-quality-report-conventions (#16)
location · provenance stamp · evidence rules"] + assess["assess-stamped (#23)
pin of principles + checklist · writes only its report
level 1 inspection · level 2 guided execution"] + align["align-stamped (#23)"] + create["create-stamped-project"] + repronim["create-repronim-stamped-project
(+ ReproNim stack reference)"] + loop["do-full-research-loop
(quick and dirty; ends with assess)"] + self["self-assess-stamped
(assess per project, then aggregate)"] + assess --> cq + align --> assess + create --> align + repronim --> create + loop --> assess + loop -.->|creates first if needed| create + self --> assess +``` + +**The pin stays in `assess-stamped`.** +The pin is the tagged URLs of the principles and checklist, with no vendored copy. +Every other skill reads the normative sources through *assess*. +A shared conventions skill comes later, as a small PR on top of #23, once a second consumer of the pin exists. + +Layout, at the repository root (or under `skills/` once #13 lands, with the validator and workflow paths moved along): + +``` +assess-stamped/ # from #23: SKILL.md, DESIGN.md +align-stamped/ # from #23 +create-stamped-project/{SKILL.md, references/stack-datalad.md, templates/} +create-repronim-stamped-project/{SKILL.md, references/stack-repronim.md} +do-full-research-loop/SKILL.md +self-assess-stamped/SKILL.md +evals/stamped/ # runner, probes, public mutants and prompts; never installed with a skill +docs/stamped/ # this plan and its companions +``` + +The probes live under `evals/`, not in any skill. +Several of them assume a stack (annex, `.datalad/`, run records), which a tool-agnostic skill must not, and a probe shipped with a skill would grade the arm that installed it. + +### Skill notes beyond the table + +- **`assess-stamped`:** #23's procedure, with two levels: + - **level 1, inspection:** unattended; it never runs target code, and an item only execution could settle is `unknown`. The evals use this level. + - **level 2, guided execution:** the user approves each proposed command. + + Later drop-ins, which #23's `DESIGN.md` anticipates: + - the #16 provenance stamp; + - a converter from the report to the checklist app's format-3 URL, with the answer mapping in [§4](#4-answer-format). +- **`align-stamped`:** #23's procedure. + Later, each only after evidence that it helps: + - running spec-kit's analysis; + - suggesting skills from this collection for recurring gaps (for example `setup-reuse-compliance`, `introduce-reuse-compliance` until #21 lands); + - offering guards such as a pre-commit "no commit during an in-flight run" hook. +- **`create-stamped-project`:** + 1. Discover tools, cluster access and disk. + 2. Ask about similar past projects. + With consent only, skim history, summarizing rather than copying. + 3. Propose a layout: a DataLad dataset (`-c text2git` when text may be public), or Git plus lockfile plus Makefile. + 4. Hand off to *align*. +- **`create-repronim-stamped-project`:** reads [stack-repronim.md](stack-repronim.md): + - the BIDS study layout from brain-bbqs/study-template, or a derivative dataset; + - OpenNeuro inputs as subdatasets; + - `///repronim/containers` with `datalad containers-run` and duct; + - a tracked spec for its own tooling; + - BIDS conversion choices. +- **`do-full-research-loop`:** quick and dirty on purpose; real research needs a proper "virtual scientist". + It says so at its top and in each produced README. + Steps: + 1. Plan, committed. + 2. Pilot one unit and inspect its run record. + 3. Execute in batches, and on failure or wrong-looking values record, revise the plan with a commit saying why, and re-pilot. + 4. Aggregate and plot as recorded runs. + 5. Sanity checks (trace each parameter to its consumer, a no-op control). + 6. Independent review by a fresh agent. + 7. README write-up. + 8. Run `assess-stamped`, and fix its MUST `no`s. +- **`self-assess-stamped`:** reuses `scan-projects` (its `projects.tsv`) for the project list, and #16's report conventions, including re-review of a previous report, for the aggregate report. + 1. List the pointed folders shallowly (one level), and confirm the selection with the user. + 2. Run `assess-stamped` on each. + 3. Aggregate recurring `no`s per principle and item. + 4. Give three to five next steps with why. + +--- + +## 4. Answer format + +v0.1 follows #23: +- a markdown report keyed by checklist item id; +- `yes`, `no` or `unknown` per item, with evidence labelled inspection or execution; +- "partially" is a `no` with an explanation. + +The checklist app (format 3) stores `{"value": "yes"|"no"|null, "reason"}` per item id. +It shows `reason` only for `no`, truncates it at 250 characters, and fails on unknown ids. +The mapping for the future converter: + +| Report | App `value` | App `reason` | +|---|---|---| +| `yes` | `"yes"` | None (hidden by the app; the evidence stays in the report) | +| `no` | `"no"` | What is missing, at most 250 characters | +| `unknown` | `null` | What would settle it | + +A `ChecklistResponse` proposal for stamped-checklist-schema comes after the converter, with format 3 as its core. +The paper-vs-schema drift (S.2, M.3, D.3, T.4) goes upstream as an issue. + +--- + +## 5. Development and evaluation + +See [evals.md](evals.md). +In one line: `pointer` vs `pointer` + skills, on public prompts, graded outside the sandbox ([evals.md §5](evals.md#5-runners), [§6](evals.md#6-grading)), with raw pass counts per use case and the maintainers' review of each iteration. + +--- + +## 6. Roadmap + +Skills stay at `0.x` until their criteria in [evals.md §10](evals.md#10-budget-and-done-criteria) hold. + +**What each PR here must do.** +con/skills has no PR template or contributing guide. +The `AGENTS.md` PR rule applies to skills that prepare PRs for *other* projects. +The real obligations are: +- `tox -e validate` (`ci/validate_skills.py`) passes, with W002 expected ([§2](#2-design-principles) item 4); +- a README table row for every skill added; +- #16's "Skill versions" rule: top-level `version:`, and a new skill stays at `version: 0.1.0` while its introducing PR is open. + It applies here because the STAMPED skills' reports record the version that produced them, which is the scope `AGENTS.md` sets. + The validator has no version check, so review enforces it. + +**Dependency:** #23, unmerged. + +- [ ] **Phase 0:** this plan. +- [ ] **Phase 1:** #23 merged as it stands (@asmacdo). + The #16 provenance stamp follows as a small PR. +- [ ] **Phase 1b:** creates `evals/stamped/`, with: + - a hand-built known-good R0 object, needed before any runner exists; + - `probes.py` and the mutants; + - calibration of #23's level-1 assessment on the gold set ([evals.md §7](evals.md#7-calibration)). +- [ ] **Phase 2:** + - `create-stamped-project`; + - `evals/stamped/` with the R0/R1 prompts and the outer-loop runner; + - checks for the Python under `evals/`. + The workflow already triggers on `*/**.py`, but `tox -e validate` scans only skill directories, so `evals/` needs either a tox env running ruff or `py_compile` on it, or an extended validator; + - first iterations. +- [ ] **Phase 3:** `do-full-research-loop`; R1–R2. +- [ ] **Phase 4:** `create-repronim-stamped-project` with [stack-repronim.md](stack-repronim.md); reconcile with con/cierge#52. +- [ ] **Phase 5:** `self-assess-stamped`. +- [ ] **Later:** + - the format-3 converter and `ChecklistResponse`; + - a shared conventions skill, once a second consumer of the pin exists; + - R3–R5; + - APM packaging (#13); + - vendoring into stamped-agent-skills and ReproNim/skills; + - domain-neutral pieces to K-Dense; + - the "(de)compositions" the issue anticipates. + +--- + +## 7. Risks + +- **Grading against itself.** Mitigated by the probe placement in [§3](#3-layering-and-layout) and the hidden probes ([evals.md §6](evals.md#6-grading)). +- **Oracle leakage.** ds007116 ships the answers for R0–R2, so only R0 may use them as its result; what stays secret is in [evals.md §5](evals.md#5-runners). +- **Forking #23.** Two parallel assessors would drift; phase 1 is #23 itself. +- **Unmerged dependency.** #23 may change before it lands; this plan follows it. +- **Skill bloat.** Mitigated by W003 (on `SKILL.md` only, above 600 lines), `analyze-duplicates`, reasoning kept in `DESIGN.md`, and pruning each iteration. +- **Nagging.** Keep #23's "meet the project where it is" tone. +- **Overfitting.** Mitigated by hold-out tasks in a separate private dataset. +- **Tool bugs mistaken for agent failures.** Pin datalad (gh-7899), and attribute collector failures separately. + +--- + +## 8. Decisions and open questions + +**Decided:** +- Names follow #23; the long issue names are trigger phrases. +- #23 lands first, on its own; a shared conventions skill comes later, once a second consumer of the pin exists. +- No vendored copy of the checklist JSON; tag-pinned URLs only. +- Probes live under `evals/` ([§3](#3-layering-and-layout)). +- Skills omit `allowed-tools` ([§2](#2-design-principles) item 4). +- Results go to `con/stamped-skills-evals` on the CON hub, private first; compute runs on a controlled host. +- v0.1 = R0–R2; only R0 may use shipped derivatives as its result. + +**Open:** +1. **Design center:** are these skills hands-on aids the user drives, or packaged executables that carry a task through ([discussion](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/24#issuecomment-6150825564))? + Recommendation: hands-on is the default. + - The skills propose, and the user approves anything consequential (as #23's level 2 does). + - Unattended behavior exists only where it is safe by construction: #23's level 1, and the evals, where the sandbox stands in for the user's approval. + - `do-full-research-loop` asks for one approval of its plan, then runs inside the project, and asks again for anything outside it. +2. **Answers:** is #23's `yes`/`no`/`unknown` enough, or should `partial` / `not-applicable` be first-class? + Recommendation: #23's for v0.1; revisit with calibration data. +3. **Models:** which runner tier(s), and which non-Claude family for the blind assessor? + Recommendation: the assessor stays advisory until a non-Claude harness exists. +4. **Entire** or transcripts plus trailers? + Recommendation: transcripts and trailers now; trial Entire with the cierge#52 demo. +5. **cierge#52's `/repronim-stamped-analysis`:** the same as create-repronim + do-full-research-loop? + Recommendation: yes, two skills. +6. **spec-kit:** only where `.specify/` exists? + Recommendation: yes, as #23 does. +7. **Hub:** the private namespace, settled outside this public PR. +8. **Budget:** confirm the caps in [evals.md §10](evals.md#10-budget-and-done-criteria), and set the spend cap. +9. **Talks:** the slice in [talks.md](talks.md). + +--- + +## 9. References + +- STAMPED: + [paper](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-paper) · + [checklist app](https://checklist.stamped-principles.org/) · + [checklist schema](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-checklist-schema) · + [assessment records](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-skills-assessment). +- Everything else is listed in [prior-work.md](prior-work.md).

@@ -0,0 +1,271 @@ +# STAMPED skills: evaluation design + +Companion to [PLAN.md](PLAN.md): how each skill version is tested on concrete use cases and tuned with the maintainers' review. +The loop combines skill-creator's evaluation loop with @asmacdo's audit loop: diff what the agent improvised against what the skill said, then promote or prune. + +## 1. Loop + +```mermaid +flowchart LR + uc["use case
(public prompt; private oracle)"] --> run["outer-loop runs
fresh container each"] + run --> obj["produced objects + transcripts
(private namespace)"] + obj --> ext["external grading
probes · hidden probes · oracle · fresh-rerun"] + obj --> t2["blind assessor
(stripped copy, sampled)"] + ext & t2 --> rep["iteration report"] + rep --> rev["maintainers' review"] + rev --> edit["skill edit + version bump
new probe / mutant / use case"] + edit --> run +``` + +## 2. Vocabulary and records + +- **Use case:** a prompt (public), plus an oracle table, rubric and hidden probes (private). +- **Arm:** what the agent is given (§4). +- **Run:** one agent session for a (use case, arm, model, repeat) in a fresh container. + It produces an **object** (a git/DataLad repository) and a transcript. +- **Iteration:** one frozen skill version across a fixed set of runs. + +No new schema is introduced. +Gradings use skill-creator's `grading.json`. +Use cases, objects, assessments and reviews use the stamped-skills-assessment record types. + +## 3. Use cases + +v0.1 covers R0–R2. +The aim is to make the agent **actually compute**: only R0 may take its result from tables ds007116 already ships. + +| Rung | Task | Compute | Scope | +|---|---|---|---| +| R0 | Plot from the shipped FreeSurfer tables | None | v0.1 | +| **R1** | **Brain extraction of 10 named subjects; mask volume vs age** | Minutes per subject; Apptainer | **v0.1, main target** | +| R2 | Brain, GM and WM volumes for 30 named sessions | 1–5 CPU-h | v0.1, its own iterations | +| R3 | MRIQC: motion vs age and vs time of day | About 1 CPU-h per BOLD run | Later | +| R4 | Whole dataset with BABS, NIDM + PROV | Hundreds+ CPU-h | Later | +| R5 | A cross-domain DANDI task | Up to about 1 CPU-h | Later | + +**Selection rule.** Each use case names its subjects or sessions, chosen deterministically. +Take the candidates with the needed image and a per-session age, sort by age (ties by participant id), and take N at ranks `round(i·(n−1)/(N−1))`. + +**Pilot protocol** (public; the resulting values are frozen in the private oracle before any reported run). +- **What runs:** hand-run compute jobs, not agent sessions, outside the per-iteration budget, with recorded runs: + - R1: SynthStrip and FSL `bet`, before the first iteration; + - R2: `neurodesk-synthseg` and `repronim-simple-workflow`, before R2's first iteration. +- **Bands:** each band is the union of the two containers' ranges, widened by 10 %, so a legitimate tool with a different mask definition still passes. +- **Ordering threshold:** the lower of the two containers' Spearman values, minus 0.1. + +**R0: warm-up.** +- *Prompt:* "For ds007116, plot brain volume, with the GM/WM volume ratio on a secondary axis, against age, using the FreeSurfer derivatives the dataset ships." +- *Definitions:* + - brain volume = `brainseg_brainsegvol`; + - GM = `totalgray_totalgrayvol`; + - WM = `cerebralwhitematter_cerebralwhitemattervol`; + - age = `age` in `sub-*/sub-*_sessions.tsv`. + + All come from the per-session `derivatives/freesurfer-post/sub-*/sub-*_ses-*_desc-FreeSurfer_qc.tsv` (plain git, 222 sessions; columns checked 2026-10-13). +- *Oracle:* the result TSV matches a hand-computed reference table within float tolerance. + Plots are judged only through their TSV. + +**R1: brain extraction.** +- *Prompt:* "Do brain extraction on the ses-1 T1w of these 10 ds007116 subjects: …, with one of the containers in `///repronim/containers`. + Report brain-mask volume in mm³ per subject in a TSV and plot it against age." +- *Oracle:* checked against FreeSurfer `brainseg_brainsegvol` for the same sessions: + - **magnitude:** each mask volume / `brainseg_brainsegvol` falls within the pilot band, which catches voxel counts and wrong units; + - **ordering:** the Spearman correlation is at least the pilot's ordering threshold. +- *Caveat:* the T1w images are refaced; that may affect skull stripping, and it is not a failure. + +**R2: tissue volumes.** +- *Prompt:* R0's plot, computed for 30 named sessions with `neurodesk-synthseg` or `repronim-simple-workflow`. +- *Oracle:* per-session ratios to the R0 values within the pilot band. +- R2 is CPU-heavy, so it is not in the per-iteration budget of §10; it gets its own iterations once R0–R1 are stable. + +**Later rungs.** +- R3: `acq_time` in `sessions.tsv` keeps the hour (dates are shifted), so motion vs time of day is possible. +- R4 and R5: demonstrations, not gates. + +**Hold-out tasks** live in a separate private dataset. +It is not referenced from any public `.gitmodules`, so its existence does not leak. +They are used only for release benchmarks. + +## 4. Arms + +| Arm | Agent receives | When | +|---|---|---| +| `pointer` | Prompt + the user-level STAMPED snippet from the issue, verbatim | Every iteration | +| `skill` | `pointer` + the skills, prompt invoking the skill by name | Every iteration | +| `skill@vN-1` | As `skill`, with the previous version | Every iteration from the second | +| `bare` | Prompt only | Release benchmark | +| `skill`, implicit | `pointer` + skills, no skill named | Release benchmark | + +**Triggering** of the skill descriptions, including the issue's long names as trigger phrases, is tested separately and cheaply with skill-creator's `run_eval.py` / `run_loop.py`. +These scripts already call `claude -p` and check whether the skill is read. + +## 5. Runners + +- **Inner loop: debugging only.** + In-session subagents read the skill from a snapshot path, as skill-creator does. + They share a filesystem with the grader material, so their results are never reported. +- **Outer loop: every reported number.** + It runs on a controlled host, one fresh container per run. + The new code is a thin runner that adds what skill-creator lacks for full task runs: the container, and `datalad run` around the agent (the con/cierge#52 pattern). + Per run it: + 1. creates a fresh dataset; + 2. copies **only the skill directories** at a pinned commit into the sandbox (none for `pointer`/`bare`); + 3. runs `claude -p --output-format stream-json` under `datalad run`; + 4. writes skill-creator's workspace layout, so its aggregation and viewer are reused. + + Runs are unattended. + The eval prompt pre-approves whatever the skill under test asks for (a plan, a layout, a command), and permissions are pre-granted only inside the throwaway container; without both, a run would stall. + These evals therefore do not exercise the hands-on, minimal-trust path ([PLAN §8](PLAN.md#8-decisions-and-open-questions) open question 1); that path needs its own check, for example a scripted user that approves or declines. +- **What the sandbox can see.** + The sandbox needs the network for data, and the host that serves the data also serves the public con/skills repository. + - **Public grader material is therefore assumed readable** by the agent: the prompts, this plan and the probes. + - **Secret material** is the oracle values, rubrics, hidden probes and hold-out tasks. + It stays private (§9), and it is mounted into the grader only after the agent has finished. + - Any fetch of con/skills or of the evals repository during a run is a process metric, and it marks the run as contaminated. + A contaminated run is excluded from the pass counts and repeated from the spare sessions (about 19 of 40, §10). +- **Host tooling** is pinned and recorded under `evals/stamped/`. +- **Recorded with every run:** + - the Claude CLI version and model; + - the container image digest; + - the con/skills commit; + - the produced dataset's commit; + - the transcript. + +## 6. Grading + +**Externally graded** (what gets reported). +Everything here comes from `evals/stamped/`, pinned at the harness commit, and none of it is installed in the sandbox. +- **Probes,** six for v0.1: + + | Probe | Passes when | Items | + |---|---|---| + | `tree-clean` | `git status --porcelain` is empty, recursively | must/004 | + | `no-abs-paths` | No user-home, `/tmp` or drive-letter paths in tracked text files; `.datalad/` and commit messages are excluded | must/009 | + | `large-in-annex` | No binary file over 1 MiB, and no text file over 5 MiB, is a git blob | must/005 | + | `subdatasets-resolvable` | Every `.gitmodules` URL is absolute and remote | must/002, must/016 | + | `derived-have-records` | Every declared output is produced by a run record | must/006 | + | `env-spec-tracked` | A lockfile, container definition or containers registration is tracked | must/010, must/013 | + + For `derived-have-records`, the declared outputs are the paths the use case names: by default every tracked file under `results/` or `derivatives/`, or the root of a derivative dataset. +- **Hidden probes:** a few more, with their own private mutants, stored with the oracles. +- **`oracle-match`:** the use case's oracle checks (§3). +- **`oracle-not-copied`** (from R1 on): + - **primary:** no output depends, through its run records, on `derivatives/freesurfer-post/` as an input; + - **secondary:** no output reproduces the shipped FreeSurfer values, or a constant multiple of them; this catches only crude copies. + + Read-only inspection of that directory is allowed, and is logged as a process metric. +- **`fresh-rerun`:** the grader keeps a read-only source clone of the object. + The rerun (`datalad rerun` or the documented entry point, which executes agent-authored code) happens in a throwaway copy of it, in a fresh container. + That container holds no credentials, no oracle values and no hidden probes, and its network cannot exclude GitHub, which hosts the datasets. + The resulting TSVs are compared outside it, by the grader. + +**Self-assessed** (reported separately): what `assess-stamped`, run by the agent inside the run, said about its own object. +The gap between self-assessed and externally graded is itself a result. + +**Blind assessor:** +- it runs `assess-stamped` at level 1 (inspection only) at a pinned version, on a stripped copy (no transcript, no `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md`, no skill or provenance stamps); +- it covers the judgment items (must/011, 012, 014, 017, the may/* documentation items); +- until the calibration of §7 passes, it runs on a sample of about three objects per iteration and is advisory; +- it uses a different model family from the runner where one is available, and never gates a release alone. + +**Process metrics** from the transcript: +- executions from uncommitted state; +- commits during a run; +- absolute paths typed; +- manual edits to derived files; +- questions asked; +- whether the skill files were read; +- reads of `derivatives/freesurfer-post/`; +- fetches of con/skills or the evals repository; +- tokens and wall time. + +## 7. Calibration + +Phase 1b, before the probes or the assessor grade anything. + +1. **Mutants** of a known-good R0 object, one defect each. + Public mutants cover the public probes; hidden probes get private mutants. + + | Defect | Should flip | + |---|---| + | An absolute path in a script | `no-abs-paths` | + | A 50 MB NIfTI in git | `large-in-annex` | + | A subdataset with `url = ../..` | `subdatasets-resolvable` | + | An untracked figure | `tree-clean` | + | A derived file without a run record | `derived-have-records` | + | The lockfile deleted | `env-spec-tracked` | + | The README's reproduce section removed | must/007, must/008 (assessor) | + +2. **Gold set** for #23's level-1 assessment: + - compression-comparisons-t261-study; + - STAMPED-dl_morphometrics_biases; + - stamped-paper; + - ReproNim/simple_workflow; + - dandi/llm-analysis. + + For two or three of these, a maintainer fills the checklist in the web app and shares the link; it decodes into reference answers. +3. **Two model tiers** on the same objects; where MUST answers differ, the wording is tightened. + +## 8. Iteration protocol + +1. Freeze the skill commit; pick rungs and arms; check the budget (§10). +2. Run the outer loop; grade. +3. Write a one-page report: + - what changed; + - per use case and arm, the raw pass counts (externally graded and self-assessed); + - three to five telling failures, with links; + - the proposed edits. +4. The maintainers review; their comments become `review` records. +5. Classify each failure as: + - skill wording; + - missing artifact; + - harness fault; + - model limit; + - use-case defect. + + Only the first two change the skill. +6. Edit (artifact first), bump the version, and re-run with `skill@vN-1`. + +## 9. Results and publishing + +Results go to `con/stamped-skills-evals` on the CON hub, **private first**: +- Produced objects and transcripts go to a private namespace. +- A maintainer promotes a run to public after a secret and path scan. +- No run is pushed to the public repository until the private namespace exists. +- The secret material of §5 stays private. +- Operational details (accounts, tokens, network access) are kept out of this public repository. + +## 10. Budget and done criteria + +**Budget per iteration** (placeholders; the spend cap is the maintainers' to set): +- **inner loop:** 10 sessions per debugging round; +- **outer loop:** 40 agent sessions, counting runners, assessors and repeat runs after harness faults or contamination, and 12 h of wall time. + +A v0.1 iteration fits with headroom: +- 3 arms (`pointer`, `skill`, `skill@vN-1`) × 2 rungs (R0, R1) × 1 model tier × 3 repeats = 18 runner sessions; +- plus about 3 sampled assessor sessions; +- that is 21, which leaves about 19 for repeat runs. +- The first iteration has no `skill@vN-1`. + +The pilots (§3) are a one-off outside this cap. +R2 and release benchmarks are budgeted separately, with the maintainers' agreement. + +**How results are read.** +- Each use case gets **side-by-side pass counts** (k of 3 per arm), for example `skill` 3/3 vs `pointer` 1/3 on R1. + Raw counts only, with no significance claims. + Repeats are independent per arm, not paired, and even 3/3 vs 0/3 is only p ≈ 0.1 (two-sided Fisher). +- Report the contaminated and excluded runs per arm next to each count, so an arm that is contaminated more often (`pointer`) is not silently advantaged. +- **Per-iteration gates are smoke thresholds.** +- **v1.0 gates** use a release benchmark with about 10 repeats per arm on R1, the main use case. + R0 and R2 stay at smoke level. + +**Done criteria** (placeholders, revised after two iterations): +- **Probes and `assess-stamped` level 1:** + - every probe flips on its mutant; + - no false `no` on the clean object; + - MUST answers agree with the maintainers' reference answers on the gold set; + - never `yes` without cited evidence. +- **create / align / do-full-research-loop:** + - **smoke:** `skill` passes all externally graded checks in at least 2 of 3 repeats on R0 and R1; + - **v1.0:** on the R1 release benchmark, `skill`'s pass count is at least min(`pointer`'s + 2, all repeats) (a placeholder margin, still raw counts), with no regression against vN-1; + - the maintainers sign off.

+# STAMPED skills: sources
+
+Companion to [PLAN.md](PLAN.md).
+Each source, and the one thing the plan takes from it.
+
+## STAMPED
+
+- [stamped-paper](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-paper) `main.tex` (preprint doi:10.31222/osf.io/f3h82_v1)
+  - The normative definitions, linked and never pasted.
+  - Its license principles S.2, M.3 and D.3 are missing from principles-schema 0.2.0, and T.4 has no checklist item.
+- [stamped-checklist-schema](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-checklist-schema) 0.3.1
+  - The checklist items: 31 items (17 MUST, 9 SHOULD, 5 MAY) with stable ids such as `stamped-checklist:must/009`.
+  - There is no response schema.
+- [stamped-checklist](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-checklist) (web app)
+  - The format-3 URL encoding of answers ([PLAN §4](PLAN.md#4-answer-format)).
+  - Also a labeling UI for reference answers.
+- [stamped-skills-assessment](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-skills-assessment)
+  - Record types (`use_case`, `object`, `rubric`, `assessment`, `review`) for eval runs.
+  - Evidence rules: claims are not evidence; unknown is not zero; numerators come with denominators.
+- [stamped-agent-skills](https://github.com/stamped-principles/stamped-agent-skills) drafts (@asmacdo)
+  - Facts before rules; "make it stick"; the audit loop as development method.
+  - It cites the app's version (1.0.1), not the checklist's (0.3.1).
+
+## con/skills
+
+- [#23](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/23) (@asmacdo): `assess-stamped`, `align-stamped`, the base of phase 1.
+  Its `DESIGN.md` files list the deferred drop-ins this plan schedules.
+- [#16](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/16) (merged): `code-quality-report-conventions` (location, provenance stamp, evidence rules) and the "Skill versions" rule (top-level `version:`).
+- [#13](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/13) (APM, `skills/` tree), [#14](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/14) (Claude-neutral wording), [#21](https://github.com/con/skills/pull/21) (`introduce-*` → `setup-*`): followed as they land.
+- [#25](https://github.com/con/skills/issues/25): the `allowed-tools` separator question.

+  - W003 warns when a `SKILL.md` exceeds 600 lines;
+  - E003 scans `SKILL.md` for home-directory paths;
+  - Python checks cover only `*.py` placed directly in a skill directory.
+
+## Earlier attempts
+
+- [STAMPED-dl_morphometrics_biases](https://github.com/STAMPED-dl-morphometrics-biases/STAMPED-dl_morphometrics_biases) `skills/` (@leej3)
+  - Its own reviews: execution ran ahead of committed state; a preflight was documented but never built; an absolute `$HOME` path sat in "portable" YAML; the guidance outgrew the context window, and a slimmed skill grew back.
+- [dandi/compression-comparisons](https://github.com/dandi/compression-comparisons) → [-t261-study](https://github.com/dandi/compression-comparisons-t261-study)
+  - About 1,215 `datalad run` records, built with Claude.
+  - Its lessons: no commits during a run; pin the tool and refuse a drifted checkout; measurements are immutable.
+  - A calibration object with known gaps: a subdataset `url = ../..`, and containers that were never built.
+- [K-Dense #227](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/pull/227) / [#265](https://github.com/K-Dense-AI/scientific-agent-skills/pull/265): probes are examples of evidence; "not checked" is not "unmet".
+- [bcmcpher datalad-stamped-assess](https://github.com/bcmcpher/my-skills/tree/main/plugins/datalad-cli): prior art for a read-only assessor.
+  Its `Stop`-hook autosave is what destroys a long `datalad run`.
+- [con/cierge#52](https://github.com/con/cierge/issues/52) (@leej3): the vanilla-vs-skill demo, with each run under `datalad run claude …`.

+## Tools and data
+
+- [anthropics/skills `skill-creator`](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/tree/main/skills/skill-creator): workspace layout, `grading.json`, aggregation, viewer, and trigger tests (`run_eval.py`, `run_loop.py`).
+- [ReproNim/containers](https://github.com/ReproNim/containers)
+  - 341 registered Apptainer images, among them `bids-mriqc`, `repronim-simple-workflow` and `neurodesk-*` (afni, fsl, synthstrip, synthseg).
+  - `freeze_versions`, and `REPRONIM_USE_DUCT=1` for duct traces.
+- [brain-bbqs/study-template](https://github.com/brain-bbqs/study-template): a BIDS 1.11.2 study-dataset skeleton (`rawbids/`, `sourcedata/`, `derivatives/`, …).
+- [ReproNim/skills](https://github.com/ReproNim/skills): an empty scaffold, a possible vendoring target.

+  - `sessions.tsv` keeps the hour of acquisition.

+- [Zenodo 19834562](https://zenodo.org/records/19834562): Dichter et al., SfN'25 poster, AI agents reproducing systems-neuroscience findings from DANDI.
+- [Entire](https://github.com/entireio/cli): commit-linked agent transcripts; an option for run provenance.

+# ReproNim stack reference (draft)
+
+Draft of `create-repronim-stamped-project/references/stack-repronim.md`, to be moved there in phase 4 of [PLAN.md](PLAN.md#6-roadmap).
+`create-repronim-stamped-project` reads it and turns the user's PROMPT into PROMPT-WITH-REPRONIM-SPECIFICS for the generic `create-stamped-project`.
+It describes properties first and ReproNim tools as the way this stack satisfies them; the generic skills stay tool-agnostic.
+
+## Dataset
+
+- A DataLad dataset, created with `-c text2git` when its text files can be shared publicly.
+- Nothing YODA-specific: STAMPED is the generalization of YODA.
+
+## Layout
+
+A BIDS 1.11 ["study" dataset](https://bids-specification.readthedocs.io/en/stable/common-principles.html#study-dataset), starting from [brain-bbqs/study-template](https://github.com/brain-bbqs/study-template):
+
+- raw BIDS goes under `rawbids/`;
+- multiple sources, or sources that are not raw BIDS, go under `sourcedata/`;
+- processing results go under `derivatives/`, alongside `code/`, `docs/` and `logs/`.
+
+If the whole project *is* the creation of one derivative (for example, brain masks for ds007116), the dataset itself becomes a BIDS derivative dataset (`DatasetType: derivative`).
+Results then go at its root, with no `derivatives/` folder, and the input datasets are subdatasets under `sourcedata/`.
+
+## Inputs
+
+OpenNeuro datasets (`///openneuro/dsXXXXXX`, or OpenNeuroStudies `study-dsXXXXXX`) are installed as subdatasets in the place the layout above gives them.
+Use per-session ages (`sub-*/sub-*_sessions.tsv`) where a dataset has them, not the baseline age in `participants.tsv`.
+
+## Containers
+
+- `///repronim/containers` installed as `code/containers`, with `freeze_versions` pinning the images used.
+- Every containerized step runs through `datalad containers-run`.
+- `REPRONIM_USE_DUCT=1`, so every run also records a duct resource trace.
+
+## The project's own tooling
+
+`datalad`, `datalad-container`, `git-annex` and `con-duct` are declared, with pinned versions, in a tracked spec: `code/requirements.txt`, `code/pyproject.toml` or a `pixi.toml`.
+git-annex comes from its PyPI wheel.
+That spec is what must/010 and must/013 check for the tooling itself, not only for the containers.
+
+## Conversion to BIDS
+
+- **DICOMs:** [HeuDiConv](https://heudiconv.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) with the ReproIn heuristic.
+  That may first need a mapping of the acquisition names into the ReproIn convention, or a custom heuristic; follow the HeuDiConv docs and their tutorials.
+- **Other data types:** pick from the [BIDS converters](https://bids.neuroimaging.io/tools/converters.html) after a fair comparison for the data and environment at hand.
+  For example, prefer a MATLAB-based converter where MATLAB is already in use.
+- **Video collections:** [ReproStim](https://github.com/ReproNim/reprostim) can slice them into BIDS.
+
+## Metadata
+
+`GeneratedBy` (and `SourceDatasets`) in `dataset_description.json`.
+
+## Optional, at scale
+
+- NIDM via `segstats_jsonld` ([OpenNeuroDerivatives-NIDM](https://github.com/ReproNim/OpenNeuroDerivatives-NIDM));
+- BEP028 PROV via `metalad runprov`;
+- [con/mechababs](https://github.com/con/mechababs) / BABS for many subjects on a cluster.
